stories.head: Anthropic ships Claude Opus 5 — now the default Opus model in Claude Code with 1M context
stories.brief: Opus 5 lands in the Python SDK and Claude Code; fast mode runs $10/$50 per Mtok.
stories.tldr: Anthropic’s Python SDK v0.120.0, dated 2026-07-24, adds the `claude-opus-5` model along with tool addition/removal blocks and tool_change events [1]. Claude Code 2.1.219 makes Claude Opus 5 the default Opus model, with 1M context and fast mode at $10/$50 per Mtok [2]. A community-maintained model timeline dates the release to July 24, 2026 and describes it as an Opus model for complex agentic coding and enterprise work, with 128K maximum output and adaptive thinking enabled by default [3].
stories.why: You build AI agents on Claude, so a default-model swap plus new tool addition/removal blocks and tool_change events changes both your agent loop’s behaviour and your per-run token bill overnight — worth re-benchmarking your harness against the $10/$50 fast-mode tier before it silently becomes your baseline.

stories.head: Alphabet Q2: revenue up 24% to $119.8 billion — and Google Cloud accelerates to 82% growth
stories.brief: Google Cloud revenue jumps 82% to $24.8B on enterprise AI; 12th double-digit quarter.
stories.tldr: Alphabet reported consolidated Q2 revenues up 24% — 23% in constant currency — to $119.8 billion, marking its 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth [1]. Google Cloud saw a meaningful acceleration, with revenues rising 82% to $24.8 billion, led by Google Cloud Platform gains across enterprise AI Solutions and enterprise AI Infrastructure as well as core GCP services [1].
stories.why: As an investor on the semiconductor and data-centre theme, an 82% Cloud print driven specifically by enterprise AI infrastructure is the cleanest read-through you get on hyperscaler compute demand — it feeds directly into your accelerator, memory and power-buildout positions.

sources.claim: Alphabet Q2 2026 consolidated revenue rose 24% to $119.8 billion while Google Cloud accelerated 82% to $24.8 billion; company raised full-year capex guidance to $195–205 billion, sending the stock lower after hours.
sources.excerpt: Consolidated Alphabet revenues increased 24%, or 23% in constant currency, to $119.8 billion, reflecting strong performance across the business and our 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth. Google Cloud saw a meaningful acceleration in growth as revenues increased 82% to $24.8 billion, led by an increase in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) across enterprise AI Solutions and enterprise AI Infrastructure, as well as core GCP services.
sources.summary: Official Alphabet Q2 2026 earnings press release filed 2026-07-22. Revenue and Cloud beat consensus but record $44.9B Q2 capex and raised FY guidance of $195–205B drove after-hours selloff (~5%). Mirrors at CNBC, GOOG 8-K (SEC) and 9to5Google all blocked by proxy; text sourced from search-engine index of official press release.

The capex guidance raise to $195–205B and after-hours stock reaction extend beyond what the excerpt covers but do not undermine the core verified figures from the authoritative source.

stories.head: Unity 7 roadmap: moving up from Unity 6 means no rebuild and no new language
stories.brief: Unity says the Unity 6 to 7 transition breaks nothing and needs no traditional upgrade.
stories.tldr: Unity’s Unity 7 roadmap announcement states that “Unity 7 will not require a traditional upgrade from Unity 6 – no rebuilding, no new language to learn, nothing broken in the transition” [1].
stories.why: You work in UE5, so this is competitive intelligence rather than a task: engine-migration cost is the single biggest switching lever in this market, and Unity explicitly removing it changes how you should read the tooling landscape you benchmark against.

sources.claim: Unity Technologies unveiled the Unity 7 roadmap at Unite Seoul on July 21, 2026, featuring shader builds up to 90% faster, near-instant Play Mode, a free MCP server for AI coding-agent integration, and a no-rebuild upgrade path from Unity 6; beta December 2026, general release Q1 2027.
sources.excerpt: Unity 7 will not require a traditional upgrade from Unity 6 – no rebuilding, no new language to learn, nothing broken in the transition.
sources.summary: Official Unity Technologies announcement at Unite Seoul keynote. unity.com proxy-blocked (egress CONNECT 403); excerpt confirmed verbatim via exact-phrase WebSearch returning unity.com as primary result. Investors.unity.com and businesswire.com press releases corroborate (both also proxy-blocked).
sources.trustReason: Unity Technologies is the origin of all claims — this is their own product announcement page. Excerpt verbatim confirms the no-rebuild upgrade path; the additional specific claims (90% faster shader builds, near-instant Play Mode, MCP server, beta/GA timelines) are not covered by the captured excerpt but derive from the same authoritative origin page, corroborated by investors.unity.com and BusinessWire per the summary. Recovery is trust-neutral. Confidence discounted modestly for the gap between the multi-feature claim and the single-feature excerpt.

stories.head: Black Forest Labs announces FLUX 3 — one model jointly trained across image, video and audio
stories.brief: FLUX 3 Video and Action open in early access; the image models follow in weeks.
stories.tldr: Black Forest Labs announced FLUX 3 on July 23, 2026, described as its newest frontier model — a unified multimodal system jointly trained across image, video and audio, extendable to action prediction for robotics [1]. FLUX 3 Video and Action entered early access immediately, while FLUX 3 Image, including Dev, is rolling out in the following weeks [1].
stories.why: For your UE5 asset and material pipeline, a single model trained jointly on image and video is the kind of tool you can wire behind a Claude agent for texture and previz generation — though this one rests on a community SDK README, so treat the specifics as provisional until Black Forest Labs’ own page is reachable.

stories.head: Epic’s Unreal plugin lets Claude Code drive the live editor — 30+ toolsets over MCP
stories.brief: Hundreds of ToolsetRegistry tools reach materials, Niagara, Sequencer and Blueprints.
stories.tldr: Epic Games’ Unreal Engine plugin for Claude Code lets you control Unreal Editor directly from Claude Code via MCP [1]. It exposes hundreds of tools through Unreal’s ToolsetRegistry across more than 30 toolsets, including actors, blueprints, materials, Niagara, Control Rigs, Sequencer, State Trees, widgets, Gameplay Ability System and automation testing [1].
stories.why: This is the exact intersection of your two workstreams — Claude agents and UE5 — and the materials toolset in particular puts your shader work under agent control instead of manual editor clicking.

sources.claim: Epic Games released v3.0.4 of the official Unreal Engine plugin for Claude Code, now listed in Anthropic’s official claude-plugins-official marketplace, exposing hundreds of MCP tools for live Unreal Editor control across 30+ toolsets.
sources.excerpt: Control Unreal Editor directly from Claude Code via MCP. Hundreds of tools exposed via Unreal’s ToolsetRegistry across 30+ toolsets: actors, blueprints, materials, Niagara, Control Rigs, Sequencer, State Trees, widgets, Gameplay Ability System, automation testing, and more.
sources.summary: GitHub repo commit on 2026-07-22 bumped plugin to v3.0.4 and redirected install docs to Anthropic’s official claude-plugins-official marketplace. README fetched directly from raw.githubusercontent.com. Commit author: Thomas Mansencal. Adds note: ‘Installing this plugin gives Claude broad, live access to the running Unreal Editor.’
sources.trustReason: Official Epic Games GitHub organization repository, README fetched directly (reachable, no recovery needed). The marketplace-listing detail is in the summary rather than the excerpt, a minor gap that keeps confidence just below maximum but does not materially undermine the core technical claims.

stories.head: Gemini 3.6 Flash surfaces in LiteLLM’s registry — 1M input context at $1.50 per million tokens
stories.brief: Registry entry lists 64K max output, reasoning support and text, image, audio, video in.
stories.tldr: LiteLLM’s model registry carries an entry for `gemini/gemini-3.6-flash` with an input cost of $1.50 per million tokens, a 1,048,576-token maximum input and 65,536-token maximum output [1]. The entry flags reasoning support and text, image, audio and video modalities, and names Google’s Gemini 3 pricing page as its own source [1].
stories.why: When you size context budgets for Claude-based agents, a rival flash-tier model at 1M input and 64K output is the comparison point for your long-context routing and cost ceilings — noting this is a community registry entry, not Google’s own announcement.

stories.head: Unity teases a first: a Unity game rendering natively inside Unreal Engine
stories.brief: PC Gamer reports a cross-engine demo putting Unity content through Unreal’s renderer.
stories.tldr: PC Gamer reports Unity previewing a cross-engine first, quoting the promise that “You will see, for the first time, a Unity game rendering natively inside Unreal Engine” [1].
stories.why: As a UE5 developer profiling with Unreal Insights, a foreign engine’s content running through Unreal’s renderer raises immediate questions about frame cost and Nanite compatibility — worth tracking, but this rests on a single secondary report with no technical detail in the quote.

sources.claim: At the Unite Seoul keynote on July 21, 2026, Unity demonstrated a Unity-simulated game rendering natively inside Unreal Engine in real time, with physics, lighting, and input synchronized between the two engines via PolySpatial; early access for developers planned for 2027.
sources.excerpt: You will see, for the first time, a Unity game rendering natively inside Unreal Engine
sources.summary: PC Gamer article covering Unity senior director James Stone’s live cross-engine demo at Unite Seoul. pcgamer.com proxy-blocked (egress CONNECT 403); excerpt confirmed verbatim via exact-phrase WebSearch returning pcgamer.com as primary result. Yahoo Tech republished the same article. Demo used a map called Fantasy Kingdom.
sources.trustReason: PC Gamer is a reputable, established gaming and game-development outlet (T2: reporting-on rather than originating). The excerpt directly supports the core claim — ‘for the first time, a Unity game rendering natively inside Unreal Engine’ — with matching same-day publication date consistent with live keynote coverage. The specific implementation details in the claim (PolySpatial, physics/lighting/input sync, 2027 early-access timeline) are not in the captured excerpt and represent extrapolation beyond the verbatim quote; those details suppress confidence slightly. Recovery is trust-neutral.

stories.head: SK Hynix seen printing a record Q2 operating margin — analysts split between 74.6% and 77%
stories.brief: Forecasts put memory margins as much as five points above the 72% Q1 record.
stories.tldr: Korea Investment & Securities expects SK Hynix’s operating margin to climb to 74.6% in Q2, while BLOTER, citing FnGuide data, offers a more bullish estimate of roughly 77% [1]. That upper figure would sit five percentage points above the previous record of 72% set in Q1 [1].
stories.why: For your semiconductor book, a memory maker holding mid-70s operating margins is the sharpest available signal that HBM pricing power has not yet cracked — the key input for how long you stay long the AI-memory complex.

sources.claim: SK Hynix is forecast to post a record Q2 2026 operating margin of 74.6–77%, surpassing its own Q1 record of 72%, driven by HBM demand; earnings due July 28–29.

stories.head: Bond markets price a one-third chance the Fed hikes at the July 28–29 meeting
stories.brief: Hawkish policymaker tone and costlier energy revive rate-increase odds ahead of the FOMC.
stories.tldr: Fixed income markets now assign roughly a one-third chance that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at its July 28-29 meeting [1]. Rising energy prices and a more hawkish tone from policymakers are keeping inflation risks front and center [1].
stories.why: A live hike risk repricing the front end hits the long-duration end of your book hardest — semiconductor and data-centre names — and a stronger dollar bleeds straight through to your ringgit-denominated Bursa positions.

stories.head: Kerjaya Prospek lands RM52.5mil job for a 275kV landing station feeding a Klang Valley data centre
stories.brief: Bursa-listed builder takes data-centre power works running through to January 9, 2027.
stories.tldr: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd has secured a subcontract worth RM52.5mil for civil, structural and basic low-voltage mechanical and electrical works in the Klang Valley [1]. The scope covers a proposed new 275-kilovolt consumer landing station for a data centre, with the contract commencing on July 23, 2026 and scheduled for completion on Jan 9, 2027 [1].
stories.why: This is your Bursa data-centre-and-energy thesis showing up as an actual signed contract rather than a narrative — grid interconnection work at 275kV is the physical bottleneck for Malaysian data-centre buildout, and it flags which listed contractors are capturing it.

sources.claim: Kerjaya Prospek secured a RM52.5 million subcontract for civil, structural, and low-voltage M&E works for a new 275kV consumer landing station serving a data centre in the Klang Valley, commencing July 23, 2026.
sources.excerpt: Kerjaya Prospek Group Bhd has secured a contract from a customer for the sub-contract for the execution and completion of civil, structural and basic low-voltage mechanical and electrical (M&E) works in the Klang Valley for RM52.5mil. The contract covers execution, completion, testing, rectification of defects and obligations for civil, structural and basic low-voltage M&E works for the proposed construction of a new 275-kilovolt consumer landing station for a data centre located in the Klang Valley. The contract commenced on July 23, 2026 and is scheduled to be completed on Jan 9, 2027.

stories.head: FBM KLCI slips a third straight session, down 0.52% to 1,711.37 as oil nears six-week highs
stories.brief: Bursa’s benchmark sheds nine points on caution over geopolitical tension and crude.
stories.tldr: The FBM KLCI ended lower for a third consecutive session on Wednesday, falling nine points, or 0.52%, to 1,711.37 [1]. The Star attributed the slide to caution amid geopolitical tensions that pushed oil prices to near six-week highs, with the index tracking mixed regional markets [1].
stories.why: Your Bursa exposure is being driven by the oil complex right now rather than by company news — worth separating the energy-driven index drag from the stock-specific data-centre stories you actually hold.
